title: Semantic Rules Schema
description: JSON Schema for semantic mapping rules in Crow-Eye Correlation Engine. This schema validates the structure and data types of semantic rules used for mapping technical forensic values to human-readable meanings.

rules.description: Array of semantic rules. Each rule defines conditions for mapping technical values to semantic meanings.

semanticRule.description: A semantic rule that maps technical forensic values to human-readable meanings. Rules can have multiple conditions combined with AND/OR logic.

rule_id.description: Unique identifier for the rule. Used for rule merging and override logic. Custom rules with the same rule_id as default rules will override the default. Use descriptive names like 'user_login_success' rather than 'rule1'.

name.description: Human-readable name for the rule. Displayed in GUI and reports. Should be concise but descriptive.

semantic_value.description: The semantic meaning/interpretation assigned when this rule matches. This is the human-readable value that replaces technical values in correlation results. Keep it concise and meaningful.

conditions.description: Array of conditions that must be evaluated. Each condition checks a specific field in a specific artifact. Multiple conditions are combined using the logic_operator (AND/OR). At least one condition is required.

logic_operator.description: Logical operator for combining multiple conditions. 'AND' requires all conditions to match. 'OR' requires at least one condition to match. For single-condition rules, use 'AND'.

scope.description: Scope of the rule application. 'global' applies to all correlations. 'wing' applies only to a specific Wing (requires wing_id). 'pipeline' applies only to a specific pipeline (requires pipeline_id). Default is 'global'.

category.description: Category classification for the rule. Used for grouping and filtering rules. Common categories include: Authentication, Execution, Persistence, Network, FileActivity, CredentialAccess, LateralMovement, Application. Optional field.

severity.description: Severity level of the rule match. Indicates the importance or threat level. 'info' for informational events, 'low' for minor issues, 'medium' for moderate concerns, 'high' for serious threats, 'critical' for severe security incidents. Default is 'info'.

confidence.description: Confidence score for the rule match, ranging from 0.0 (no confidence) to 1.0 (absolute confidence). Higher values indicate more reliable matches. Use lower values for generic or ambiguous rules. Default is 1.0.

description.description: Detailed description of the rule. Explain what the rule detects, why it's important, and any relevant context. This helps users understand the rule's purpose. Optional but highly recommended.
examples: Detects PowerShell process creation with encoded commands, often used by attackers to obfuscate malicious code
Successful user logon event (Windows Event ID 4624)
Modification to registry Run keys, commonly used for persistence

wing_id.description: Wing ID if scope is 'wing'. This rule will only apply when the specified Wing is executed. Leave empty or omit for global rules. Optional field.

pipeline_id.description: Pipeline ID if scope is 'pipeline'. This rule will only apply when the specified pipeline is executed. Leave empty or omit for global rules. Optional field.

_requires_multi_indicator.description: Multi-indicator validation flag. When set to true, this rule requires at least _min_indicators conditions to match before triggering. This reduces false positives for generic patterns that could match many unrelated applications. Use for rules with broad regex patterns or ambiguous indicators. Default is false for backward compatibility. Optional field.

_min_indicators.description: Minimum number of independent indicators (conditions) that must match for this rule to trigger. Only applies when _requires_multi_indicator is true. Must be >= 1 and should be <= the number of conditions in the rule. Common values: 2 for dual-indicator validation, 3 for high-confidence matches. Default is 1. Optional field.

_pattern_specificity.description: Pattern specificity score ranging from 0.0 (very generic) to 1.0 (very specific). Used internally to assess pattern quality. Generic patterns (e.g., '.*', '.+', '\w+') have low specificity and should use multi-indicator validation. Specific patterns (e.g., 'CHROME\.EXE') have high specificity. This field is typically calculated automatically but can be set manually. Default is 1.0. Optional field.

rule_type.description: Evaluation strategy. 'match' (default) is the flat AND/OR condition rule. 'absence' fires when expected evidence is present but required-absent evidence is missing. 'sequence' matches ordered steps within per-step time gaps. 'threshold' fires on >= min_count occurrences within a window.

condition_groups.description: Optional nested boolean groups combined with the rule's top-level logic_operator, enabling (A AND B) OR (C AND D) expressions alongside the flat conditions list.

absence.description: Spec for rule_type='absence'. Fires when every expect_present condition matches and no require_absent condition matches (optionally within within_minutes of an anchor).

threshold.description: Spec for rule_type='threshold'. Fires when matching rows occur at least min_count times, optionally within within_minutes and grouped by group_by.

sequence.description: Spec for rule_type='sequence'. Fires when the ordered steps occur in order with each consecutive gap within max_gap_minutes. Each step is a condition or {conditions:[...]} and may span different feathers. When join_fields is set, the matching records of every step must share those field values (e.g. same host/user) — a true cross-feather correlation rather than mere time-coincidence.

join_fields.description: Field name(s) that must match across the chosen record of every step (cross-tool aliasing applies, e.g. host/Computer/hostname).

technique_id.description: MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs this rule maps to (e.g. T1021, T1070.001).

tactic.description: MITRE ATT&CK tactic slugs this rule maps to (e.g. lateral-movement, defense-evasion).

eye_authorship.description: Provenance populated when EYE creates/edits the rule. Null for built-in/human-authored rules.

disabled.description: When true the rule is retained in configuration but skipped during evaluation.

condition.description: A single condition that checks if a specific field in a specific artifact matches a value using a specified operator. All fields are required.

feather_id.description: ID of the feather/artifact this condition applies to. Must match the artifact source name in your data. Common values include: SecurityLogs, Prefetch, Registry, FileSystem, NetworkLogs, ApplicationLogs. Case-sensitive.

field_name.description: Name of the field to match within the artifact. Must match the actual field name in your data. Common examples: EventID, CommandLine, executable_name, KeyPath, FilePath, RemotePort. Case-sensitive.

value.description: Value to match against the field. For 'equals' and 'contains' operators, this is a literal string (case-insensitive). For 'regex' operator, this is a regular expression pattern. For 'wildcard' operator, use '*' to match any non-empty value. Always a string, even for numeric values.

operator.description: Match operator. 'equals'/'contains'/'regex'/'wildcard' as before, plus ordered comparisons ('greater_than','less_than','greater_equal','less_equal') and 'not_equals' (NULL-safe). Comparisons work numerically or on ISO-8601 timestamps.

negate.description: When true the condition matches only when the underlying comparison does NOT hold. Used for absence / must-not-be-present logic.

compare_to_feather.description: Cross-feather comparison: draw the right-hand side of the comparison from this feather's record instead of 'value'. Requires compare_to_field.

compare_to_field.description: Field on compare_to_feather to compare against (e.g. amcache.sha1, mft $FN time). Enables masquerade / timestomp checks.
